title: Ethiopian Ful Medames
community: Urban Ethiopia — the Nile tradition of fava bean breakfast
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Ful — cooked fava beans mashed with olive oil, lemon, garlic, cumin, and tomato. The breakfast tradition that crossed the Nile from Egypt and Sudan into Ethiopian urban eating culture — served with injera or bread.
longDesc: Ful Medames is not indigenous Ethiopian but has become deeply embedded in Ethiopian urban breakfast culture through the country's connection to Egypt and Sudan via the Nile. The fava bean preparation, seasoned with lemon, garlic, and cumin, is served in tej houses and breakfast spots across Addis Ababa.
ingredients: 2 cans (800g) cooked fava beans — or 2 cups home-cooked
¼ cup fresh parsley or coriander
steps: Warm fava beans in a pan over medium heat.
Mash roughly — about half should be mashed, half whole.
Add olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, and cumin. Stir well.
Top with diced tomatoes and herbs.
chefTips: Half-mash — the mixture of mashed and whole beans is the characteristic texture.
Lemon is generous — the acidity is essential.
commonMistakes: Over-mashing to a paste — wrong texture.
cookingScience: See ETH130 for fava bean science.
sustainabilityTips: Fava beans fix nitrogen in soil.
culturalNote: Ethiopian ful is a beautiful example of how a food culture absorbs external influences — the ancient Nile Valley fava bean tradition, carried south into Ethiopia through trade and migration, has become part of the urban Ethiopian breakfast without ever losing its North African character.
